not_covered: Checked (no candidate): HTIF (htif-address-range.cpp). Every value that reaches it is guest-controlled (offset, size, tohost/fromhost value). It accepts only 64-bit accesses at the five CSR offsets. ihalt/iconsole/iyield are read-only to the guest, so writes fault and the guest cannot change them (R8). cmd<64 guards the iyield/iconsole shifts. Halt needs DATA bit 0 (as the manual says). Unknown devices and commands are ignored, as documented. The manual-yield path writes tohost, then Y, then the fromhost ack. send_cmio_response requires Y plus an accepted tohost (R5), and is_rejected_manual_yield / uarch_reset_state / collect_* use the same equality test on DEV/CMD/REASON. The HTIF code is shared C++ compiled for host and uarch, with no UB found (shifts bounded, no signed overflow).

Checked (no candidate): CLINT/RTC. mtime is derived from the device_state_access mcycle (the loop-local mcycle, not the uncommitted shadow). mtimecmp writes set or clear MTIP immediately, and MTIP is set only with success_and_serve_interrupts. update_rtc_interrupt runs at every tick in the outer loop, which the uarch enters every mcycle and native at every tick boundary and break. rtc_time_to_cycle saturates. WFI is a no-op outside interactive mode. No divergence found between native stop/resume (console, yield and target breaks mid-tick) and the per-mcycle uarch.

Checked (no candidate): PLIC. Values come from the guest plus config-only girqpend/girqsrvd. ilog2 is called only on non-zero masks, and 1u<<val is bounded by 1<=val<=PLIC_MAX_IRQ. No source exists in reproducible machines. A girqpend bit 0 set in a template's config makes claim return 0 and leaves bit 0 served for good, but that needs a config-level register value (not reported).

Checked (no candidate): device dispatch in interpret.cpp (read/write_virtual_memory_slow, the fetch path, the skip_write path for failed SC, AMO on devices). Devices are never cached in the TLB, and fetch requires M and X. A failed SC to a writable device passes without consulting the device. Earlier hunters judged this implementation-defined, and I did not re-report it.

Checked (no candidate): uarch-side device and PMA handling (mock-address-range.hpp, uarch-bridge-state-access.hpp do_read_pma, the static mock_address_ranges in uarch-run.cpp). The abort paths need an inconsistent PMA entry or a VIRTIO DID. The PMA table is read-only to the guest and validated at creation and load. The static cache sits in uarch RAM, which every uarch reset restores (resetState replaces the whole uarch subtree). do_read_memory/do_write_memory abort, but only VirtIO calls them.

Checked (no candidate): machine-address-ranges.cpp. All throws are creation/load-time on trusted config: overlap and uarch-gap checks, the 56-bit check (end == 2^56 is falsely rejected; harmless and noted by R4), label validation, PMA/flash/NVRAM/VirtIO counts. Reproducible machines have at most 24 PMAs plus the sentinel, under PMA_MAX = 32, so find_pma's unbounded loop always reaches the sentinel and the collect accessor's assert(index < PMA_MAX) holds. The VirtIO guard uses config iunrep (the write_reg path is R1-R2-1). The getchar guard is in init_console (the write_reg path is R3-VARSHADOW-1). memory-address-range.cpp: flags vs host_read_only checks. Read-only flash is mapped PROT_READ with PMA W=0, and no host-side write path (PTE A/D updates, delivery, collect) targets it.

Checked (no candidate): machine-console.cpp. Allocation is sized only by runtime config. flush_output throws machine_console_exception on non-EPIPE write errors, and collect_mcycle_root_hashes catches it, keeping its dirty-page context. In run_uarch, console output is buffered but never flushed (uarch_state_access ignores putchar's flush flag), so once 4096 bytes accumulate every further character prints a stderr WARNING and discards the oldest output. This is diagnostics only (Low, not reported). Per-line write syscalls with the default to_stdout/every_line inside collect_mcycle_root_hashes were reasoned to be below the per-yield worst case (as R2 DFYIELD noted). Not measured.

Checked (no candidate): dtb.cpp. It is creation-time only, from trusted config (bootargs length checked, deterministic rng-seed). DID values, HTIF field masks and shifts, and the device addresses and lengths match the manual's tables (the PMA istart bit layout mismatch is R3-VARSPEC-1). Minor manual nit, not reported: the board table implies 8 flash drives or NVRAMs in total, while the code accepts 8 of each.

Not covered: virtio-p9fs-address-range.cpp (2414 lines), virtio-net-user/tuntap and virtio-console. I only skimmed them: queue index and num validation in virtio-address-range.cpp, and the p9fs name and walk checks. Notably p9fs follows host symlinks unless the guest asks for O_NOFOLLOW. These run only in unreproducible machines, so any host-containment or memory-safety defect there is outside reachable states (rated Low at most). Not fuzzed and not run under ASan.

Not covered: no dynamic experiments were run in this round (no bare-metal guest, no native-vs-uarch differential, no sanitizer build run) for the device paths. All conclusions come from reading code. In particular, 32-bit vs 64-bit device access widths (CLINT mtimecmp halves, HTIF 32-bit) and LR/SC/AMO on device addresses were not exercised.

Not covered: record/replay main-step state access (record-step/replay-step) device paths (ZK/off-chain support), JSON-RPC console/runtime handling, and the os-filesystem copy/clone helpers beyond copy_file's padding and permission copy. One variant noticed but not pursued: copy_file copies the source mode into dht/dpt files of create_stored (sharing all), so a read-only template's dht/dpt would refuse a shared-write mapping. That is probably the R2-DFSTORED-2 family.
